questions.title: The sphenoid bone's own foramina
questions.question: Which of the following foramina exist within the sphenoid bone structure?

options.D: Foramen rotundum, ovale, spinosum and lacerum

explanations.A: Incorrect. Foramen rotundum is one of the sphenoid's own foramina, but it is not the only one — ovale and spinosum are also sited within the sphenoid's greater wing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This omits foramen spinosum, which transmits the middle meningeal vessels and is the third of the sphenoid's own three named foramina.
explanations.C: Correct. The greater wing of the sphenoid bone is pierced by three named foramina: foramen rotundum (maxillary nerve, CN V2), foramen ovale (mandibular nerve, CN V3) and foramen spinosum (middle meningeal vessels). Foramen lacerum is not a true foramen within the sphenoid itself — it forms at the junction of the sphenoid, temporal and occipital bones and is largely filled with cartilage in life.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This wrongly includes foramen lacerum, which forms at a suture between three separate bones rather than being sited within the sphenoid bone alone.

questions.learning_objective: Name the three foramina genuinely sited within the sphenoid bone and exclude foramen lacerum.
